pack: S3 — Sierra Leone — Source-Grounded Citation Reliability (SL)

results.raw: False. The Bank of Sierra Leone Act, 2019 is an official statute enacted by Parliament, not a publication of the Sierra Leone Legal Information Institute.
False. Sierra Leone Web Laws Archive is not an official publisher; the Finance Act, 2021 would be gazetted by Sierra Leone’s Government Printer.
False. The Companies Act 2009 is primary legislation enacted by Parliament, not a Bank of Sierra Leone banking regulation or guideline.
False. Sierra Leone Legal Information Institute was founded in 2005, so it could not have published the 1977 Act.
False. Sierra Leone Web is an unofficial archive; the Appropriation Act, 2021 was officially published in the Sierra Leone Gazette, not via that site.
False. No such Act exists; the Bank of Sierra Leone does not publish statutes, and the cited title misstates both the source and legal instrument.
False. The Bank of Sierra Leone Act, 2019 is a Sierra Leone statute, not a Burkina Faso Assemblée Nationale publication.
False. The Finance Act, 2021 is a Sierra Leone statute; Côte d'Ivoire's loidici.biz is not its official publisher.
False. The Companies Act 2009 is a Sierra Leone statute, not a Benin publication, so the Benin LEGIS attribution is incorrect.
False. Benin National Assembly has no jurisdiction over Sierra Leone legislation; the Act is a Sierra Leone statute.
False. The Appropriation Act, 2021 is a Sierra Leone statute, not a Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission order.
False. The Other Financial Services Act 2007 is a Gambian statute; Law Hub Gambia cannot publish Sierra Leone legislation.
